preamble: Depalatalization of a palatalized velar [kʲ] to plain [k] removes the secondary palatal articulation and typically merges the palatalized series with the plain velars. The best-known case is the 'centum' merger of Indo-European, in which the Proto-Indo-European palatovelar *ḱ (usually interpreted as [kʲ] or a fronted velar) fell together with plain *k in Italic, Greek, Celtic, Germanic and Tocharian. Even in the satem branches, Balto-Slavic shows sporadic or conditioned depalatalization of *ḱ to k, as in Lithuanian akmuõ 'stone'.

examples.note: The PIE palatovelar merged with plain *k in Proto-Italic (*kəntom), giving Latin initial /k/.
Proto-Hellenic *hekətón shows the same merger of *ḱ with *k.
Via Proto-Celtic *kantom, with plain /k/ from the PIE palatovelar.
Tocharian, though geographically eastern, is a centum branch: Proto-Tocharian *känte.
A satem language that otherwise turns *ḱ into š; here the palatovelar was depalatalized to k (compare the doublet ašmuo and Sanskrit aśman). Latvian akmens shows the same k.
